newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Lehman keeps Teva buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Lehman keeps Teva buy.

text.p: Israel's Teva Pharmaceutical Industries was rated a 1-buy in a report released on Monday by Lehman Brothers.
"Excellent results confirm robustness of base business, leaving room for upside earnings surprises, excluding contribution from the multiple sclerosis drug Copaxone," analyst Richard Silver said.
Lehman reiterated its buy rating, saying the sales ramp-up of Copaxone remained the key catalyst for the stock.
It said the pending U.S. commercial launch of Copaxone remained on track with shipments expected to begin this month and formal selling efforts in late March.
Silver said Teva shares were trading at 20 times Lehman's 1997 estimated earnings of $3.00 per share and 12 times its 1998 estimate of $4.90 a share. He gave Teva a price target of $70.00.
He estimated earnings per share for first quarter 1997 would be $0.50 compared with $0.31 a year earlier.
"We see the opportunity for capital appreciation in 1997 as Teva's growth rate accelerates during the next year," Silver said.
